name: Sidebar
description: Persistent primary-workspace navigation that preserves destination identity and current-route context across expanded and compact presentation. Sidebar owns the named navigation region, grouping, mode presentation, and optional supplemental footer; the application shell owns placement and responsive mode choice, while the product/router owns destination data and current location.

props.name: mode
props.description: Persistent navigation presentation. Expanded shows icon plus destination label; compact keeps the same destinations as icon targets with retained accessible names.

props.name: label
props.description: Short navigation-region/group label. It is visible in expanded mode and remains the navigation accessible name in compact mode.

props.name: items
props.description: Required ordered destination data containing 1–8 entries. Each entry has a stable id, non-empty label, href, and compatible icon; Sidebar renders only the governed internal _Navigation Item anatomy.

props.name: currentId
props.description: Required destination id identifying exactly one current route. Sidebar derives aria-current and selected presentation from this id.

props.name: footer
props.description: Optional supplemental workspace/account context rendered after flexible space. It is not a second primary-navigation region and should contain no more than two direct content children.

representations.mapsTo: publicApi.currentId compared with each item id
inherited Light/Dark token context; no theme prop

anatomy.name: navigation
anatomy.description: Named persistent nav region containing the optional visible expanded group label and ordered destination list.

anatomy.name: group-label
anatomy.description: Short visible contextual label in expanded mode; compact mode retains it as the nav accessible name without visible text.

anatomy.name: items
anatomy.description: Ordered list of 1–8 private _Navigation Item renderers.

anatomy.name: flexible-space
anatomy.description: Flexible region that keeps the optional footer anchored toward the logical block end without adding route semantics.

anatomy.name: footer
anatomy.description: Optional supplemental workspace/account content region with up to two direct children.

anatomy.name: logical-end-border
anatomy.description: One-pixel subtle border on the logical inline end, automatically mirroring in RTL.

semantics.element: named native nav containing an ordered list of native destination links
semantics.accessibleName: The non-empty label names the primary workspace navigation in both expanded and compact modes.
semantics.keyboardActivation: Native anchor behavior supplied by the internal _Navigation Item; Sidebar adds no custom roving-tabindex or arrow-key model.
semantics.focus: Destination links remain in logical document order and use native tab order; the persistent Sidebar does not trap focus.
requirements: Sidebar requires 1–8 destination items. Empty navigation and more than eight destinations are rejected because they exceed the governed Figma slot boundary.
Every item requires a stable unique non-empty id, non-empty destination label, non-empty href, and compatible icon.
currentId must match exactly one destination id so exactly one current route is exposed in the navigation region.
Destination identity and order remain the same when mode changes between expanded and compact presentation.
The same current route remains discernible when mode changes; compact presentation never hides the selected destination from assistive technology.
The navigation region is named in both modes. Expanded mode renders the short group label visibly; compact mode retains that label as the accessible navigation name.
The current destination exposes aria-current=page through the internal native link and no non-current destination exposes aria-current.
Keyboard focus follows the destination list in logical source order and Sidebar never introduces a focus trap, backdrop, modal behavior, or Escape policy.
The Figma authority fixes expanded Sidebar width at 208 CSS pixels and compact Sidebar width at 64 CSS pixels.
The expanded internal item source is 184 by 40 CSS pixels with a 40px minimum target height; compact items are 44 by 44 CSS pixels.

Expanded mode uses a 30px top inset and 12px inline inset; compact mode uses a 48px top inset and 10px inline inset. These Component / Layout values remain private component layout decisions rather than public token API.
The navigation list uses an 8px gap, the expanded group-to-list section gap is 18px, and the logical end border is 1px using the semantic subtle border color.
Footer content is supplemental workspace/account context only, accepts up to two direct children by convention, and cannot be used to bypass the governed primary destination list.
Application Shell owns physical placement and responsive mode selection; Sidebar does not expose a breakpoint, drawer/open state, placement, or collapse-control API.
Product/router code owns route configuration and navigation effects; Sidebar renders native href destinations and does not own routing state transitions.

navigation.description: Ordered destination data is rendered only through the private _Navigation Item implementation so mode/current/accessibility behavior cannot drift per consumer.

footer.description: Supplemental workspace/account context. Prefer no more than two direct children and never use it for unrelated primary routes.
